title: When the Uniform Turns
premise: In 1911, in the river-port city of Vhalen, sixteen-year-old Lior Quintana—indentured since childhood to the Meridian Trading Company after her pearl-diver parents drowned—believes history is something that happens to other people. When an infant is abandoned at the company warehouse with a note reading 'forget the face,' Lior hides the child and discovers the baby is the last heir of a deposed merchant dynasty the company helped destroy, and that her own indenture papers were forged from that same fallen house's records. As company men close in and a rigged inquiry prepares to bury the truth, Lior races to enter testimony into the city's official record before the river ice breaks and the winter court adjourns—knowing that speaking will cost her freedom, and silence will cost her soul. She wins the record but loses her name to it, ending the book years later as the child, grown, reads aloud the testimony of 'the unnamed depositor' and gives Lior back her history.
about_author: Quentin Villalobos is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloging shipping ledgers from defunct trading companies. Their fiction excavates the lives recorded only as marginalia.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Opening on the frozen river and the warehouse where she tallies pearls she'll never own; establishes her philosophy that history happens elsewhere. Emotional beat: quiet resignation mistaken for contentment.

chapters.title: Indenture Papers
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Clerk Odile Voss reviews Lior's contract, noting oddities in its provenance Lior has never been allowed to see. Beat: first hairline crack in Lior's acceptance of her place.

chapters.title: A Bundle at the Door
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. During a whiteout night, a dying woman leaves an infant at the warehouse door with the note 'forget the face.' Lior, alone on watch, takes the child inside. Beat: terror fused with a fierce, unfamiliar protectiveness.

chapters.title: Forget the Face
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile discovers the note and, instead of reporting it, burns it—revealing she recognizes something. Beat: complicity offered like a hand extended over a chasm.

chapters.title: The Company's Winter
chapters.summary: Warehouse master Brann Hesk's POV. The Meridian Company prepares its annual audit; Hesk suspects inventory discrepancies and orders the docks searched. Beat: menace arriving in the language of paperwork.

chapters.title: Milk and Ledgers
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior smuggles the baby between counting rooms, learning from a laundress how to feed her. Naming her Nell in secret. Beat: tenderness blooming inside danger.

chapters.title: What the Divers Knew
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Visiting her parents' old diving community, Lior hears fragments about the Aurelian family—a merchant house drowned in debt and scandal nine years ago. Beat: grief reopening as curiosity.

chapters.title: The Face in the Miniature
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile compares the baby's locket portrait to a company archive miniature of Lady Serevan Aurelian. The child is the heir everyone believes dead. Beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Hesk Counts Twice
chapters.summary: Hesk's POV. Hesk finds a second blanket fiber and narrows his suspicion to the night watch. He interviews Lior, who lies for the first time in her life. Beat: the sick thrill and shame of deception.

chapters.title: The Ice Road Inquiry
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. News arrives that the magistrate's winter court will hear 'matters of estate' until the ice breaks—weeks away. Odile explains what testimony on the record means legally. Beat: hope acquiring a deadline.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Flashback chapter: Odile as a young clerk who filed the falsified seizure documents against House Aurelian under duress. Beat: guilt as a slow poison.

chapters.title: A Buyer for Silence
chapters.summary: Hesk's POV. A company director offers Hesk promotion for delivering 'the loose thread' quietly. Hesk, ambitious and hollow, accepts. Beat: villainy revealed as banality.

chapters.title: The Laundress's Price
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The laundress Marta, caught helping, demands Lior retrieve her brother's confiscated boat license from company files. Beat: survival shown as a web of debts, not virtue.

chapters.title: Into the Archive
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Night infiltration of the records vault; Lior finds her own indenture file bears a seal belonging to House Aurelian. Beat: vertigo—her identity was never hers.

chapters.title: Whose Child Was I
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior confronts Odile with the seal. Odile admits the Quintanas were Aurelian retainers; their drowning during the seizure was never investigated. Beat: rage and mourning colliding.

chapters.title: The River Keeps Its Dead
chapters.summary: Diver elder Yorick's POV. The diving community remembers the night the Aurelian barges went down; Yorick saw men cut lines. Beat: witness memory as buried ammunition.

chapters.title: Testimony Is a Weapon
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile coaches Lior on how sworn deposition works—and how easily victors' historians rewrite records afterward. They must file before the ice breaks. Beat: strategy replacing panic.

chapters.title: Nell Runs a Fever
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The baby falls gravely ill; a doctor visit risks exposure. Lior chooses the doctor. Beat: love forcing risk over caution.

chapters.title: The Doctor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Doctor Imre Pell's POV. Pell recognizes Aurelian features and quietly notes the visit—an entry that could save or doom them. Beat: the terrifying neutrality of strangers.

chapters.title: Hesk Sets a Trap
chapters.summary: Hesk's POV. Hesk leaks word that the vault will be unguarded, baiting whoever took the fibers. Beat: the hunter's patience.

chapters.title: Martа's Brother
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Retrieving the boat license, Lior is nearly caught by Hesk's clerks; Marta's brother ferries her across broken shore ice. Beat: solidarity among the indebted.

chapters.title: What Odile Burned
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Hesk confronts Odile about the missing note; she deflects but knows he'll return. Beat: fear sharpening loyalty into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Deposition Drafted
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In the loft, by candlelight, Lior writes everything: the seizure, the drowning, the heir, her forged papers. Beat: authorship of self through testimony.

chapters.title: A Witness Comes Forward
chapters.summary: Yorick's POV. Yorick agrees to swear the divers' account—but insists his whole community sign, refusing lone-hero history. Beat: collective courage against individual legend.

chapters.title: The Audit
chapters.summary: Hesk's POV. The directors arrive; Hesk uses the audit to lock down the warehouse and post guards at the magistrate's hall. Beat: the net tightening with bureaucratic calm.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Counting Room
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A fellow indentured boy, Tam, sells information to Hesk to buy out his own contract. Beat: the price of survival paid by someone else's freedom.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Ice
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. With guards coming, Lior flees across the freezing river carrying Nell, guided by Marta's brother's knowledge of thin ice. Beat: pure physical peril; motherhood forged in flight.

chapters.title: Sanctuary of the Divers
chapters.summary: Yorick's POV. The diving community shelters Lior and Nell below in the ice-houses; elders debate whether truth is worth the reprisal. Beat: communal deliberation, no easy answers.

chapters.title: Odile's Confession
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile surrenders herself to the magistrate voluntarily, filing her own deposition about the falsified seizures, drawing Hesk's attention. Beat: redemption purchased with ruin.

chapters.title: The Broken Bargain
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam realizes Hesk never intended to honor his buyout; hollowed, he brings Lior word of the hearing schedule. Beat: the betrayer's bitter education.

chapters.title: The Last Day of Ice
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Dawn of the final day of session. Lior dresses Nell in the Aurelian locket and walks toward the magistrate's hall past Hesk's guards. Beat: terrible calm before the plunge.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Inside, Lior swears her deposition publicly, presenting Nell and the seal; Odile's filing corroborates; Yorick's community signs as witnesses. Beat: climax—the voice breaking the victors' silence.

chapters.title: Hesk Unravels
chapters.summary: Hesk's POV. Confronted with sealed originals Odile preserved, Hesk's careful paper trail turns evidence against him; the directors disown him. Beat: the machine devouring its own.

chapters.title: The Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. That night the river cracks and groans open, the winter court adjourns, and the record stands. Lior weeps on the bank—not triumph, but exhaustion. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: What Freedom Costs
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The inquiry voids her forged indenture but the company's lawyers stall restitution; Lior is free and penniless, working Marta's laundry line. Beat: victory without reward.

chapters.title: Odile's Sentence
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile receives a reduced sentence for cooperation and asks only one visitor: Lior. Their reconciliation is imperfect and real. Beat: forgiveness as unfinished work.

chapters.title: An Heir, Decided Otherwise
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Aurelian distant kin claim Nell; Lior must fight not for custody but for Nell's right to know her story—and wins a promise of letters. Beat: letting go as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Unnamed Depositor
chapters.summary: Nell's POV (years later, 1929). Grown Nell, now an archivist herself, finds the deposition credited to 'the unnamed depositor' and traces the laundress's descendants to find Lior, old and alive. Beat: history recovered by the next generation.

chapters.title: Her Name Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. In the reading room, Nell enters a correction to the record restoring Lior Quintana's name, then travels to meet her. Beat: grace, earned slowly.

chapters.title: When the Uniform Turns
chapters.summary: Alternating Lior and Nell POV. On the unfrozen riverbank where her parents dove, Lior tells Nell the whole story at last; the uniform of servitude long turned, identity passes on not as blood but as told truth. Beat: resolution—inheritance completed.
